question: to the Commission Manuela Ripa (PPE), Tomáš Zdechovský (PPE), Dan-Ştefan Motreanu (PPE), Liudas Mažylis (PPE), Eleonora Meleti (PPE), Jagna Marczułajtis-Walczak (PPE), Elena Nevado del Campo (PPE), Alex Agius Saliba (S&D), Vytenis Povilas Andriukaitis (S&D), Ondřej Krutílek (ECR), Elisabetta Gualmini (Renew), Ciaran Mullooly (Renew), Majdouline Sbai (Verts/ALE), Mounir Satouri (Verts/ALE), Sebastian Everding (The Left), Merja Kyllönen (The Left) Subject:

At a time when the EU is facing growing mental health challenges and increasing pressure on healthcare systems, hearing health remains insufficiently integrated into prevention and mental well-being strategies. Yet untreated hearing loss affects more than 57 million EU citizens and is closely linked to social isolation, depression and cognitive decline. Hearing loss is also considered the leading modifiable risk factor for dementia, with the potential to reduce individual dementia risk by up to 8 %. Despite the availability of effective and affordable solutions, many people requiring hearing care remain untreated. Strengthening prevention, early detection and access to care could therefore play an important role in supporting healthy ageing, improving quality of life and reducing the long-term burden on healthcare systems across the EU. In the light of the ‘Healthier Together’ initiative, can the Commission clarify the following: 1.
How does the Commission plan to strengthen prevention and early detection of hearing loss across Member States?
What actions will the Commission take under EU4Health and related initiatives to improve access to hearing care and reduce environmental factors contributing to hearing loss?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.8.2026) 1. The Commission supports Member States and stakeholders in the prevention and management of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) via the 2022 ‘Healthier Together’ EU NCDs initiative1, which recognises hearing loss as a factor contributing to dementia. In May 2026, the Commission adopted a communication Enhancing the Strategy for the Rights of Persons with Disabilities up to 2030, which reinforces its commitment to building a Union where the rights and dignity of persons with disabilities are fully realised. The strategy pays attention to accessibility as an enabler of rights2. In December 2025, the Commission proposed the revision of the EU legislative framework for medical devices, which also applies to hearing aids3. The revision will simplify procedures while maintaining patient safety and public health protection. 2. The Commission has provided financial support on dementia from the EU4Health programme4 to support collaborative work between Member States and stakeholder-led projects. Under the joint action PreventNCD5 (EUR 76 million), Member States collaborate on developing and implementing prevention policies on NCDs and their risk factors. The joint action JADE-Health6 (EUR 4,5 million) aims to reduce the burden of dementia and other neurological disorders by transferring best practices from the EU Best Practice Portal on Public Health7. The project Care4Elders8 (EUR 450 000) works on transforming dementia through innovative, digital, and person-centred approaches. Through the European Research Council the Commission also funds research in hearing and audio-based diagnostics.
